Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Business coverage is dominated by the fallout from the US midterm elections, which triggered a historic tech/AI stock selloff and is reshaping expectations for the AI data-center buildout, alongside Anthropic's push to proceed with its IPO roadshow despite the volatility. Geopolitical friction with China (sanctions retaliation, Nvidia's Jensen Huang) and the dramatic collapse of Paraguay's government over a bank scandal are also drawing heavy cross-outlet attention.

stories.headline: AI stock rout deepens after Democrats' midterm sweep
stories.summary: Tech stocks suffered their worst day since the 2025 tariff panic, with the Nasdaq Composite falling 5.5% and the semiconductor index plunging 12.3% as investors reassessed AI data-center spending after Democratic wins in Texas, Ohio and Georgia governor's races that threaten new restrictions on data centers.

stories.headline: Anthropic presses ahead with IPO roadshow despite market volatility
stories.summary: Anthropic plans to proceed with formal investor marketing for its IPO next week, following two weeks of tech-stock volatility tied to massive AI spending plans and the Democratic midterm landslide; FT reports the Claude maker is still targeting a roughly $1.5 trillion valuation and a pre-Thanksgiving listing.

stories.headline: Paraguay's president removed and arrested after bank collapse
stories.summary: Santiago Peña was impeached, removed from office and placed under house arrest after a bank with close ties to his administration collapsed, rattling a South American economy that had drawn heavy foreign investment and close US ties.

stories.headline: Tesla to wind down Cybertruck production to make way for Cybercab
stories.summary: Elon Musk said Tesla will stop building the Cybertruck at its Texas Gigafactory around the middle of next year to free up capacity for its driverless Cybercab, after the polarizing pickup failed to hit mass-market sales and drew repeated recalls.

stories.headline: US intelligence probed Nvidia CEO Huang over alleged ties to Chinese spy
stories.summary: American intelligence reportedly warned that Nvidia's Jensen Huang had been involved with an executive recruited by China to gather information on the chipmaker, a story with major implications for US-China tech tensions.

stories.headline: Beijing vows retaliation over new US sanctions on Chinese firms
stories.summary: China's Ministry of Commerce said it opposes new US sanctions on two Chinese companies and reserves the right to take countermeasures, as FT separately reports Washington is warning Beijing it must immediately meet its Busan trade-deal commitments on rare earths.

stories.headline: Wendy's rejects Trian's $1.4 billion takeover bid
stories.summary: Wendy's board unanimously rejected a $1.4 billion offer from Nelson Peltz's Trian Fund Management to take the burger chain private, saying the bid undervalues its turnaround prospects despite seven straight quarters of declining same-store sales.

stories.headline: Fox closes $22 billion deal to buy Roku
stories.summary: Fox completed its $22 billion acquisition of Roku, a deal the Washington Post says will give Fox a significant edge in free, ad-supported streaming.

Business.gaps: Puck had no business-relevant items identified in search or feed; Business Insider and Politico (beyond midterms politics coverage) yielded no distinct business leads in the available feed/search results.

US politics.overview: Coverage across these outlets is dominated by the fallout from Tuesday's historic Democratic midterm sweep, especially Trump's decision to replace Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller as chief of staff, alongside a wave of analysis on what Democrats will do with newfound power in Congress and the states, GOP soul-searching, and market jitters over AI investment tied to the election results.

stories.headline: Trump replaces Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller as chief of staff
stories.summary: Axios reports Trump installed hardline aide Stephen Miller as chief of staff after blaming Wiles for the midterm losses, calling it a sign he may double down on the hardline policies that cost Republicans Congress rather than moderate.

stories.headline: GOP wrestles with whether there will be any reckoning after midterm wipeout
stories.summary: Politico reports that Miller's promotion to chief of staff has deepened Republican fears that the party won't undergo a genuine reckoning after its historic midterm defeat.

stories.headline: Democrats plot what to do with newfound power after historic wave
stories.summary: Stateline reports that Democrats' sweeping state-level wins will give the party new control over governments nationwide, setting up fights over long-sought policy changes, while Roll Call separately notes Democrats in Washington face early tests over using the veto and filibuster.

stories.headline: Midterms blow open the 2028 presidential map, rattling Republicans
stories.summary: Politico reports that strategists on both sides now see states like Ohio, Texas and Iowa as competitive for 2028, a shift that has GOP operatives panicking about the party's future map.

stories.headline: AI stocks tumble as investors fear Democratic Congress will curb data center boom
stories.summary: The Washington Post reports investors are dumping AI-linked stocks on fears that a Democratic-controlled Congress could slow data center construction, with global markets sliding as they process the election's potential impact on the AI boom.

stories.headline: Supreme Court takes up Goldman Sachs arbitration case as DOJ intensifies Dobbs leak probe
stories.summary: SCOTUSblog reports the Court granted review in a Goldman Sachs arbitration dispute, part of a busy November sitting that also includes the Justice Department stepping up its investigation into the Dobbs opinion leak.

stories.headline: DOJ drops lawsuit over California's disputed ballots after repeated court losses
stories.summary: Courthouse News reports the Justice Department dismissed its suit seeking to force California to set aside roughly 20,000 disputed ballots after failing to persuade three courts, including the Supreme Court, to require citizenship verification.

stories.headline: Democratic statehouse wins put Medicaid expansion back on the table in holdout states
stories.summary: Stateline reports that in several holdout states, Democrats appear poised to use their newly won statehouse majorities to expand Medicaid under the Affordable Care Act.

US politics.gaps: NOTUS: no stories from the last 24-48 hours were found via search; available results were weeks to months old. Politico, NYT, WSJ and The Guardian coverage reflects only the provided feed items since these outlets block web search.

Tech & AI.overview: Coverage is dominated by the fallout from OpenAI's new $11 billion funding round at a $1.25 trillion valuation and Anthropic's parallel push toward a blockbuster IPO, both unfolding against a backdrop of post-midterm market jitters over the AI trade. A second major thread involves US-China tech security tensions, including allegations that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had a relationship with an alleged Chinese spy and new scrutiny of chip exports to China.

stories.headline: OpenAI raises additional $11 billion at $1.25 trillion valuation
stories.summary: OpenAI has reportedly raised an additional $11 billion as part of a funding round that hasn't closed yet but is expected to in the coming weeks, cementing its status as one of the world's most valuable private companies.

stories.headline: Anthropic presses ahead with IPO targeting $1.5 trillion valuation
stories.summary: Anthropic intends to list before Thanksgiving despite a brutal tech rout, with The Information reporting the company plans to proceed with its formal investor roadshow next week after filing its S-1 with the SEC.

stories.headline: Wall Street's all-in AI bet blows up after midterm elections
stories.summary: Democrats' historic midterm victories sparked a hedge fund and retail investor exodus from the AI trade that had dominated equity markets, with WSJ describing systematic trades that amplified the losses before stocks recovered some ground Friday.

stories.headline: China reportedly recruited AI executive to spy on Nvidia's Jensen Huang
stories.summary: China's Ministry of State Security allegedly enlisted Megaspeed executive Alice Huang to gather intelligence on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, and FT reports US officials believe the two had a romantic relationship.

stories.headline: US cleared Nvidia chip exports to Chinese firms with troubling ties
stories.summary: The Commerce Department approved dozens of Chinese companies to handle Nvidia's H200 chips, with some of the approved firms having ties to entities already under US sanctions over national security concerns.

stories.headline: Tesla to end Cybertruck production, refocus on Cybercab
stories.summary: Elon Musk said Tesla will stop producing the electric Cybertruck by mid-2027 to make room for increased production of its autonomous Cybercab ride-share vehicle.

stories.headline: Hundreds of Chinese-made AI hacking tool instances found exposed online
stories.summary: Security researchers at Censys discovered over 800 publicly exposed copies of ARTEX, an AI-powered open-source penetration testing tool linked to several cyberattacks since July, left accessible to anyone on the internet.

stories.headline: METR finds Anthropic may have crossed its own AI acceleration warning threshold
stories.summary: Nonprofit auditor METR spent eleven weeks reviewing Anthropic's internal research data and concluded the pace of model development has roughly doubled, with about 80 percent of the speedup driven by AI-assisted research itself.

Tech & AI.gaps: Platformer and VentureBeat had no distinct breaking stories in the last 24-48 hours beyond older items surfaced in search (VentureBeat's most recent relevant item was from October 28). Google DeepMind's official blog shows no new announcements within the last two days. The Verge, Wired, Ars Technica, WSJ, FT, The Economist, and NYT were only checked via the provided feed items since they block general web search.

Energy.overview: Coverage is dominated by the fallout from this week's U.S. midterm elections and what it means for energy and climate policy, utility regulation, and data-center-driven power demand, with Heatmap, Latitude Media and Utility Dive all converging on this theme. A second cluster centers on COP31 and climate science (a fast-developing 'super El Niño' and falling Chinese emissions), while WSJ and FT cover utility rate shocks and geopolitical energy implications of the U.S. election.

stories.headline: Democrats' midterm sweep set to reshape U.S. energy and climate policy
stories.summary: Heatmap's lead political analysis argues that a decisive Democratic midterm victory effectively ends the Trump administration's anti-renewables push and will usher in a more moderate, affordability-focused energy politics rather than a return to aggressive decarbonization messaging.

stories.headline: Blue wave delivers rebuke to monopoly utilities over rate hikes
stories.summary: Latitude Media reports that voters in Georgia and Michigan punished utilities over rate increases and political spending, with separate pieces noting Democratic governors won by campaigning on protecting ratepayers and that voters showed hostility toward data centers.

stories.headline: Utilities press ahead with data-center-driven capex plans after election
stories.summary: Duke Energy said it will stick with its $103 billion, data-center-fueled spending plan despite a 'historic' election, while Sempra separately flagged a 20% increase to Oncor's capex plan and DTE expanded its five-year investment plan by 30% after selling an unregulated subsidiary.

stories.headline: Berkshire Hathaway utility seeks historic 57% California rate hike
stories.summary: Pacific Power, owned by Berkshire Hathaway, is asking California regulators for a rate increase that would raise a typical residential bill by about $120 a month.

stories.headline: 'Simply staggering' super El Niño on track to peak in December
stories.summary: Carbon Brief reports a rapidly intensifying 'super El Niño' is on course to peak at the end of 2026, pushing average global temperatures higher, a development The Economist's climate newsletter also flagged as a major concern for the months ahead.

stories.headline: China's quarterly CO2 emissions post largest drop since Covid
stories.summary: A Carbon Brief analysis finds China's CO2 emissions fell 3.1% in the third quarter of 2026, the steepest quarterly decline since the pandemic, linked in part to the fallout from the Hormuz crisis.

stories.headline: Tracking the negotiating texts at the COP31 climate summit
stories.summary: Carbon Brief is running an interactive tracker following the draft legal texts being negotiated by countries at the COP31 UN climate summit.

stories.headline: Trump's election defeat could trigger a US retreat from the Middle East
stories.summary: FT argues that American political retrenchment following Trump's midterm defeat could shift the Middle East balance of power and open opportunities for China, with implications for global energy flows.

Energy.gaps: No current coverage could be found from E&E News, whose site indicates it has stopped publishing new content and folded into POLITICO Pro, or from Argus Media. Reuters, WSJ, NYT and The Economist block search, so coverage from them is limited to the feed items provided, and no NYT items were included in that feed.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage is dominated by escalating US-China trade friction ahead of the Trump-Xi summit in Shenzhen, with Washington pressing Beijing on rare earths and sanctions retaliation, alongside major Hong Kong political and legal developments including Joshua Wong's sentencing and Taiwan's diplomatic rupture with Papua New Guinea. Business and tech outlets are tracking China's AI investment boom, market stabilization efforts by the PBOC, and fallout from new US sanctions and chip export controversies.

stories.headline: US, China trade chiefs hold call ahead of Trump-Xi summit in Shenzhen
stories.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent pressed Beijing to fully implement its Busan trade commitments on rare earths and agriculture, warning that continued progress depends on concrete results, ahead of Trump's planned meeting with Xi in Shenzhen later this month.

stories.headline: Beijing vows to hit back against US sanctions on Chinese companies
stories.summary: China's Commerce Ministry said it firmly opposes new US sanctions on two Chinese companies over alleged Cuba-related dealings and reserves the right to take necessary countermeasures to protect its interests.

stories.headline: US believes Nvidia's Huang had romantic relationship with alleged Chinese spy
stories.summary: American intelligence reportedly warned that Nvidia chief Jensen Huang was involved with an executive recruited by China to gather information on the tech group.

stories.headline: U.S. Cleared Nvidia Chips to Chinese Firms With Empty Offices and Troubling Ties
stories.summary: The Commerce Department approved dozens of Chinese companies to handle Nvidia's H200 chips, with some of those firms reportedly having ties to entities already under US sanctions over national security concerns.

stories.headline: Joshua Wong sentencing: Local gov't, police, officials hail 10-year jail term amid condemnation from foreign gov't's, NGOs
stories.summary: Jailed Hong Kong pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong was sentenced to 10 years' imprisonment after pleading guilty to conspiring to collude with foreign forces, his second conviction under a national security law, drawing praise from local officials and condemnation abroad.

stories.headline: Taiwan to close representative office in Papua New Guinea, withdraw staff
stories.summary: Taiwan's foreign ministry said it will shut its Port Moresby office and halt LNG purchases after PNG renewed demands for staff to leave, accusing Beijing of using political and economic pressure to restrict Taiwan's international space.

stories.headline: China's Central Bank Pledges More Support to Stabilize Markets
stories.summary: PBOC Governor Pan Gongsheng outlined plans to broaden channels for long-term investment and strengthen state investor Central Huijin's role as a market stabilizer following a series of declines in mainland stocks.

stories.headline: Indebted tycoons haunt China's banking system
stories.summary: Chinese lenders are grappling with a hangover from years of freewheeling private-sector lending as indebted tycoons' troubles ripple through the financial system.

China.gaps: Sixth Tone, China Media Project, Rest of World, China Daily, Xinhua, CGTN, and Yicai Global did not return distinct recent results via search or feed items in this window; Reuters, AP, WSJ were not independently searchable and only appeared via other outlets' citations.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Coverage across Gulf and Middle East outlets is dominated by the ongoing US-Iran conflict, with fresh American strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island this week and intense diplomatic activity from Qatar and Gulf states to prevent full-scale war after Trump's midterm setback. Houthi-Saudi hostilities, Gaza's deepening humanitarian crisis, and several Gulf business and energy investment stories round out the agenda.

stories.headline: US carries out fresh 'minor' strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island
stories.summary: Trump confirmed new limited US strikes on Iranian air defenses on Qeshm Island, the first military action since the Republican Party's stinging midterm defeat, as Iran claimed to have downed a US drone and Gulf leaders held a flurry of calls to prevent escalation.

stories.headline: Qatar says US-Iran mediation continues despite doubts
stories.summary: Qatar's prime minister said Doha's mediation efforts between Washington and Tehran remain active to prevent the region from spiraling into wider war, pushing back on reports that talks had collapsed as Iran reviews a new nuclear proposal.

stories.headline: Trump's advisers split over whether to resume the Iran war
stories.summary: Vice President JD Vance and Gulf allies are urging Trump to wind down the conflict with Iran, while other White House advisers are pressing for renewed strikes, leaving the president's next move unresolved.

stories.headline: Houthi and Saudi-led coalition strikes escalate in Yemen and near Riyadh
stories.summary: Houthi media said Saudi strikes killed 11 people, including women and children, in Yemen's Sanaa province, while the Saudi-led coalition reported intercepting a Houthi cruise missile fired toward the Riyadh region.

stories.headline: Rains flood Gaza's displacement camps as war death toll keeps climbing
stories.summary: Gaza's Civil Defence said it received 1,500 distress calls in 10 hours as a storm swept through displacement camps, compounding a crisis in which the war's death toll has continued to rise according to medical sources.

stories.headline: Saudi Arabia releases $400m to help rebuild Syria's essential sectors
stories.summary: The state-backed Saudi Fund for Development signed loan agreements worth over $400 million with Syria's finance ministry to support energy, water, health, housing and digital infrastructure, building on more than $6 billion pledged last year.

stories.headline: Abu Dhabi property transactions jump 76% to Dh171bn
stories.summary: Abu Dhabi's real estate market recorded a sharp 76% jump in transaction value to Dh171 billion in the first nine months of 2026, underscoring continued investor appetite despite regional turmoil.

stories.headline: UAE plans up to $55bn in energy infrastructure investment
stories.summary: The UAE's energy minister said the country plans AED150-200 billion ($41-55 billion) in energy infrastructure investment by 2030, spanning renewables, nuclear and gas, as it seeks to shore up supply security after the Iran war exposed vulnerabilities.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: No distinct recent coverage was found from Zawya. Reuters, AP, FT, NYT, WSJ, The Economist and BBC block web search, so only the provided feed items were used for those outlets.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: African outlets are converging on a wave of post-election and judicial turmoil across the continent, from Tanzania's opposition trial verdict to South Africa's municipal elections and a deepening political crisis in Somalia, alongside continuing economic stories on Ethiopia's rebased GDP, Dangote's regional expansion, and Chinese/Gulf infrastructure investment. Sudan's worsening humanitarian catastrophe also features heavily across multiple outlets.

stories.headline: Tanzania's Tundu Lissu cleared of treason but jailed for inciting unrest
stories.summary: Tanzanian opposition leader Tundu Lissu was sentenced to four years in prison for inciting unrest, avoiding the treason charge that could have carried the death penalty, in a case that has drawn intense scrutiny of the country's courts.

stories.headline: Political chaos deepens in Somalia after court ruling against president's term extension
stories.summary: Somalia's opposition has accused the president of sending troops to arrest the Supreme Court's chief justice after the court declared his term extension unlawful, escalating a constitutional crisis.

stories.headline: South Africa's ANC extends its election decline but vows a Lula-style comeback
stories.summary: The ANC's support fell further in South Africa's local government elections, though it remains the largest party and some leaders believe a comeback like Brazil's Lula is still possible; African Business separately reported the party is on track for its worst-ever municipal result as opposition parties gain ground in cities.

stories.headline: UN warns millions fleeing Sudan's war lack shelter as hunger crisis deepens
stories.summary: The UN says roughly 15.4 million people displaced by Sudan's conflict urgently need shelter and household items, but humanitarian agencies are hampered by funding shortfalls; Al Jazeera and Mining Weekly (citing Reuters) separately reported worsening child malnutrition and food insecurity from drought and conflict in the south.

stories.headline: Ethiopia's rebased $201bn economy brings a bigger tax bill, not more borrowing power
stories.summary: Addis Ababa says a GDP rebasing confirms Ethiopia as sub-Saharan Africa's third-largest economy, but economists say the new figure mainly raises tax obligations rather than improving growth or borrowing prospects; Africa Confidential separately noted that Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's upbeat economic messaging is being tested by renewed fighting in the north.

stories.headline: Namibia's president takes personal charge of Dangote's $2.5bn fuel project
stories.summary: President Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah says she will personally oversee Dangote's fuel storage and regional pipeline investment, determined not to let bureaucracy cost Namibia another major project.

stories.headline: China and Gulf states tighten grip on Africa's ports and logistics
stories.summary: Africa Confidential reports that port and railway deals led by China and the UAE are promising cheaper trade and investment but also giving foreign operators growing leverage over the continent's commercial arteries, with the EU, Saudi Arabia and the US lagging behind.

stories.headline: Nigeria's central bank moves to tie every crypto P2P payment to a bank transaction
stories.summary: The Central Bank of Nigeria is introducing new rules requiring crypto peer-to-peer payments to be linked to bank transactions, tightening its oversight of who moves money through these platforms.

Africa.gaps: Could not independently verify current coverage from Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, NYT or WSJ beyond what appeared in the provided feed, since these outlets block web search; The Continent had no recent Africa-specific items available beyond its general newsletter description.

Media.overview: Coverage across media-industry outlets is dominated by the fallout from the 2026 midterms: record election-night TV ratings, a shake-up atop Trump's White House, and newsroom soul-searching over political coverage. A second cluster of stories centers on the AI-and-publishing fight, from Meta's retreat on scraping terms to a looming Times-OpenAI settlement, alongside notable business moves like Fox's completed Roku acquisition and NYT subscriber growth.

stories.headline: Trump ousts Susie Wiles, taps Stephen Miller as chief of staff after midterm drubbing
stories.summary: CBS's 60 Minutes landed the first Trump interview since the midterms, in which he previewed staff firings hours before announcing Susie Wiles' exit; CNN's Kaitlan Collins described the resulting West Wing mood as a knives-out scramble.

stories.headline: NBC tops midterm election-night ratings as overall audience jumps 23%
stories.summary: Nielsen figures show NBC News led all networks with roughly 6.7 million primetime viewers for midterm results, while total viewership across outlets rose sharply from the last midterms; The Hollywood Reporter noted broadcast networks captured the majority of the audience over cable.

stories.headline: CBS staffers blame network brass amid Trump administration's attack on 60 Minutes
stories.summary: Status reports that irate CBS News staffers are privately accusing network leadership of throwing journalists under the bus after the Trump administration targeted a 60 Minutes report.

stories.headline: New York Times adds 420,000 digital subscribers in three months
stories.summary: The Times' CEO credited strong subscriber growth to investment in human-made journalism and product experiences, a rare bright spot in an otherwise tough ad market.

stories.headline: What could the Times buy with an OpenAI settlement?
stories.summary: Puck reports the New York Times' copyright suit against OpenAI and Microsoft is heading toward a likely multi-billion-dollar settlement after a November 20 reply-brief deadline, with legal experts calling the Times' case especially strong and speculating about what an M&A war chest could fund.

stories.headline: Fox Corp completes $22 billion acquisition of Roku
stories.summary: Roku will be folded into Fox Digital Platforms alongside Tubi, Fox One and Red Seat Ventures, with Deadline separately noting the Justice Department laid out the commitments behind its approval of the deal.

stories.headline: Meta pauses controversial terms of service after publisher backlash
stories.summary: Meta indefinitely delayed proposed commercial terms that would have let it scrape Meta Business account websites, saying it is pausing the changes to engage further with stakeholders; Digiday's media briefing noted publishers remain furious over the plan even as they feel unable to walk away from the platform.

stories.headline: Russell Brand found guilty, press freedom seen as vindicated
stories.summary: Press Gazette argues the guilty verdict against Russell Brand vindicates the original Sunday Times investigation, recounting how a defence barrister swore at a reporter outside court during the trial.

Media.gaps: No current material found for NYT or The Guardian; both block direct web search and had no relevant items in the provided feed for this period.
